overview:
Organisation of Modern Languages K–10

The diagram (Figure 1) is an overview of the Modern Languages K–10 Syllabus. It shows that:

  • communication is the central goal in language learning
  • the 3 focus areas are interacting, understanding texts and creating texts
  • knowledge of language systems is applied in all focus areas and is an essential part of communication
  • intercultural capability is the capacity to exchange, understand and create meaning between people and across languages and cultures and is developed in all focus areas.

Across a stage of learning all focus areas need to be taught.

Creating written texts supports learning

The development of the Modern Languages Syllabus follows Recommendation 2: ‘Clarify and strengthen writing content in syllabus documents’ from Teaching Writing: Report of the Thematic Review of Writing (NESA 2018).

Creating written texts facilitates learning as it promotes explicitness, encourages the integration of ideas, supports reflection, fosters personal engagement and aids learners to think about the significance and implication of ideas. Each subject has particular and specific writing demands relevant for communicating within and about the discipline. Writing about content enhances understanding across subjects and stages.

The secondary curriculum includes:

  • systematic development of expectations for creating written texts which align with the English K–10 Syllabus (2022)
  • explicit writing content to support students to become fluent creators of texts and to deepen their understanding of the subject area
  • opportunities to practise the process of creating written texts to develop and communicate knowledge, understanding and ideas
  • a focus on development of word consciousness and precise use of subject-specific terminology.

Creating written texts refers to the act of composing and constructing a text for a particular purpose, audience and context.

Various methods of transcription may be employed, and a student’s preferred communication form(s) should be considered when teaching.

Syllabus framework

The Modern Languages K–10 Syllabus is organised as a framework that can be used to teach any modern language in New South Wales. A modern language refers to any language that is currently in use. There are separate syllabuses for Aboriginal Languages, Auslan and Classical Languages.

Learner proficiency

Students come to the learning of languages with diverse linguistic and cultural profiles. This may include a heritage in a particular language and/or a range of prior language experiences, either in the target language or another language.

overviewSections.heading: Access content points
overviewSections.html:
Access content points have been developed to support students with significant intellectual disability who are working towards Early Stage 1 outcomes. These students may communicate using verbal and/or nonverbal forms.

For each of the Early Stage 1 outcomes, access content points are provided to indicate content that students with significant intellectual disability may access as they work towards the outcomes. Teachers will use the access content points on their own, or in combination with the content for each outcome. 

Decisions regarding curriculum options for students with disability should be made in the context of collaborative curriculum planning.

overviewSections.heading: Life Skills outcomes and content
overviewSections.html:
Students with disability can access the syllabus outcomes and content in a range of ways. Decisions regarding curriculum options should be made in the context of collaborative curriculum planning.

Some students with intellectual disability may find the Years 7–10 Life Skills outcomes and content the most appropriate option to follow in Stage 4 and/or Stage 5. Before determining whether a student is eligible to undertake a course based on Life Skills outcomes and content, consideration should be given to other ways of assisting the student to engage with the Stage 4 and/or Stage 5 outcomes, or prior stage outcomes if appropriate. This assistance may include a range of adjustments to teaching, learning and assessment activities.

Life Skills outcomes cannot be taught in combination with other outcomes from the same subject. Teachers select specific Life Skills outcomes to teach based on the needs, strengths, goals, interests and prior learning of each student. Students are required to demonstrate achievement of one or more Life Skills outcomes.

overviewSections.heading: Protocols for collaborating with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Communities
overviewSections.html:
NESA is committed to working in partnership with Aboriginal Communities and supporting teachers, schools and schooling sectors to improve educational outcomes for young people.

It is important to respect appropriate ways of interacting with Aboriginal Communities and Cultural material when teachers plan, program and implement learning experiences that focus on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Priorities.

Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property (ICIP) protocols need to be followed. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ICIP protocols include Cultural Knowledges, Cultural Expression and Cultural Property and documentation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ identities and lived experiences. It is important to recognise the diversity and complexity of different Cultural groups in NSW, as protocols may differ between local Aboriginal Communities.

Teachers should work in partnership with Elders, parents, Community members, Cultural Knowledge Holders, or a local, regional or state Aboriginal Education Consultative Group. It is important to respect Elders and the roles of men and women. Local Aboriginal Peoples should be invited to share their Cultural Knowledges with students and staff when engaging with Aboriginal histories and Cultural Practices.

overviewSections.html:
The amount of content associated with a given outcome is not necessarily indicative of the amount of time spent engaging with the respective outcome. rationale:
Learning a language provides students with an opportunity to communicate and engage with the world and its people. Students learn the target language by developing and applying their knowledge of the language and culture(s). Studying a language enhances communication with speakers of the target language and equips learners with intercultural capability. They engage with the linguistic and cultural diversity of the world and develop respect, openness and empathy.

Students explore the target language and culture(s) and their own heritage, language(s) and culture(s). This enriches a student’s understanding of themselves and their sense of belonging as they are exposed to new ways of seeing their own identity and culture(s). The Modern Languages K–10 Syllabus invites students to consider the perspectives of others and the world beyond themselves, contributing to their own social and emotional development. Learning a language provides students with opportunities to engage socially, culturally and economically in the community. They develop a deeper understanding of their place in the world and the importance of global citizenship.

Learning a language improves literacy outcomes in first and additional languages and it also increases metalinguistic awareness. Learning languages strengthens collaborative and problem-solving skills, and enhances reflective, critical and creative thinking.

The communicative, intercultural and intellectual benefits of language learning reach beyond the individual. Proficiency in languages is a resource that serves communities and supports and promotes social cohesion within Australia. It strengthens intercultural capability, and enables students to exchange and negotiate meaning within and across languages and cultures, both locally and globally. Students develop their communicative competence and ability to use the target language in real situations and see language learning as offering valuable skills for life.
aim:
The aim of Modern Languages K–10 is to empower students to become effective communicators in the target language by developing linguistic competence and intercultural capability.

Students:

  • learn to interact, understand and create texts in the target language
  • reflect on and understand their own and others’ languages, cultures and identity
  • develop an interest in and enjoyment of language learning.

contentGroups.title: Creating multimodal texts in the target language

items.text: Create texts reproducing modelled vocabulary with visuals and other forms of nonverbal communication to express meaning
items.examples:
Beginner: contribute to group stories and performances using drama or actions.
Intermediate: describe orally what they see or hear using simple vocabulary, gestures or mime.
Advanced: create a simple card using a model.

items.text: Represent an idea or information about themselves using modelled vocabulary, formulaic phrases and visuals
items.examples:
Beginner: draw a visual of themselves and trace, copy or reproduce an accompanying target language greeting.
Intermediate: match vocabulary for introducing themselves to a visual.
Advanced: create a sentence about themselves using sentence starters, vocabulary walls, picture glossaries and/or alphabet or sound charts.

items.text: Label objects and caption images
items.examples:
Beginner: role-play vocabulary or create or select images to represent the target language vocabulary.
Intermediate: use modelled vocabulary to describe objects or visuals, such as name, size, colour.
Advanced: draw a picture and/or construct a sentence in the target language, using modelled vocabulary, by ordering, matching, selecting, clicking and dragging, repeating, tracing or copying.

contentGroups.title: Understanding and responding to target language texts

items.text: Follow simple instructions
items.examples:
Beginner: follow a simple instruction with cues, visuals and gestures.
Intermediate: follow simple instructions in classroom routines.
Advanced: follow multi-step classroom instructions.

items.text: Listen to, read and/or view simple texts such as stories or songs by participating in shared activities
items.examples:
Beginner: listen to a song following cues or visual images and repeat vocabulary in the song.
Intermediate: listen to or view a target language version of a familiar story and connect aspects of the story to their own lives.
Advanced: read or follow a picture book or multimodal text then make connections to themselves and share information.

items.text: Use auditory cues, gestures, visuals and other forms of nonverbal communication to understand texts
items.examples:
Beginner: use actions, mime, visuals or gestures to represent new vocabulary and understand a story.
Intermediate: point to, click, trace or label visuals, vocabulary and/or phrases.
Advanced: make connections with vocabulary and phrases from classroom routines, word walls, images and labels, calendars and the classroom environment to understand a text.

Respond to simple texts using actions, drawing and singing in the target language and/or English
items.examples:
Beginner: sing and respond to familiar songs or chants with miming and gestures.
Intermediate: re-enact a target language story with puppets, props and actions reproducing vocabulary to emphasise key points.
Advanced: sequence pictures to describe the order of events of a familiar story and provide an oral description.

items.text: Reproduce vocabulary seen or heard in texts to demonstrate understanding
items.examples:
Beginner: reproduce numbers to at least 10 in the target language from a text and play a card matching game.
Intermediate: draw and label a picture with vocabulary in response to a text.
Advanced: answer questions using key vocabulary and formulaic expressions from a text to share information about themselves.

contentGroups.title: Developing intercultural understanding through target language texts

items.text: Understand that there are many languages and cultural practices that are used by peers, family and community
items.examples:
Beginner: explore the different languages spoken by class members and recognise the different sounds and ways of saying greetings compared to the target language, the local Aboriginal Language and/or English.
Intermediate: observe similarities and differences of daily routine activities from various cultures, including target language culture(s) and local Aboriginal Cultures, shown in multimodal texts and draw a picture of their own experiences.
Advanced: recognise countries are represented on maps, noticing where the target language is the national language and understanding language may be spoken in additional countries, including Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Communities.

Beginner: use symbols or signing to represent familiar vocabulary when sharing information about themselves, such as age, family, pets.

Intermediate: use modelled phrases to express likes or dislikes.

contentGroups.title: Applying knowledge of the target language culture(s) to interact

contentGroups.title: Exchanging and negotiating meaning to interact in the target language

items.text: Socialise with peers to build and maintain relationships
items.examples:
Beginner: exchange information about themselves.
Intermediate: give and respond to compliments and congratulations.
Advanced: express sympathy or regret, and make amends.

items.text: Make arrangements with peers
items.examples:
Beginner: request and grant permission for an event.
Intermediate: give and respond to invitations.
Advanced: establish and negotiate guidelines for the completion of actions.

items.text: Understand and reciprocate detailed information about their own and others’ personal worlds
items.examples:
Beginner: ask for and provide detailed information on topics of personal significance such as friends and lifestyles.
Intermediate: convey facts about events in different timeframes such as the past, present or future.
Advanced: convey detailed information on a specific topic of interest.

items.text: Express and compare emotions and personal preferences
items.examples:
Beginner: convey feelings about favourite people, places or things.
Intermediate: share and explain feelings of happiness, pain or surprise.
Advanced: express and justify feelings of concern for other people.

items.text: Ask questions, make requests and explain actions
items.examples:
Beginner: ask for, give and follow a sequence of instructions.
Intermediate: ask for, give and respond to advice, and explain choices.
Advanced: persuade someone to change their point of view.

items.text: Discuss and justify opinions, ideas and perspectives
items.examples:
Beginner: ask about and express a point of view.
Intermediate: share and justify satisfaction and dissatisfaction.
Advanced: explain and clarify a personal stance on a specific issue.

items.text: Use and adapt a range of communication strategies to facilitate and sustain interactions in a range of contexts
items.examples:
Beginner: ask for clarification or confirmation and provide suggestions.
Intermediate: manage turn-taking in group activities.
Advanced: offer to explain or clarify to restore communication and facilitate conversation in group activities.

contentGroups.title: Applying knowledge of the target language culture(s) to interact

items.text: Adjust and adapt language that is appropriate to cultural practices, values and perspectives to interact
items.examples:
Beginner: use polite forms and show awareness of politeness conventions.
Intermediate: use appropriate language for avoiding and managing misunderstandings in interactions.
Advanced: adjust register of language to convey meaning in unfamiliar situations.

contentGroups.title: Understanding and responding to spoken, written and multimodal target language texts

items.text: Listen to, read and view information, ideas and perspectives in moderately complex texts on a range of themes
items.examples:
Beginner: texts such as a voicemail to explain a change of plans.
Intermediate: texts such as a multimodal advertisement promoting the benefits of recycling.
Advanced: texts such as an article addressing an issue of global significance.

items.text: Use comprehension strategies to interpret and analyse information, ideas and perspectives in texts
items.examples:
Beginner: activate, use and share prior knowledge to summarise a text.
Intermediate: use contextual clues to translate and explain a text.
Advanced: summarise and explain inferred meaning in a text for others.

items.text: Respond to texts critically and creatively in the target language and/or English by interpreting and analysing information, ideas and perspectives
items.examples:
Beginner: a personal response to an interview with a well-known person from a target language-speaking country.
Intermediate: a comparative response to interviews with well-known people from a target language-speaking country.
Advanced: an evaluative response to discuss perspectives in texts and to explain own conclusions based on the information.

items.text: Demonstrate understanding of the context, purpose and audience in texts
items.examples:
Beginner: identify and explain how vocabulary, phrases and gestures are used to emphasise key points in texts in order to achieve purpose.
Intermediate: identify cultural references in texts and examine their effect on the audience.
Advanced: identify and analyse language techniques used in texts in order to achieve purpose.

contentGroups.title: Applying knowledge of language systems to understand and respond to target language texts

items.text: Use knowledge of a wide range of features of the sound system to understand texts
Use knowledge of a wide range of sound–symbol correspondences to understand and respond to texts
Use knowledge of vocabulary from a wide range of themes to understand and respond to texts
Use knowledge of and manipulate a range of structures and features of the grammatical system to understand and respond to texts
Use knowledge of a range of structures and features of the target language writing system to understand and respond to texts
Use metalanguage to reflect on and evaluate target language structures and features in texts
items.examples:
Beginner: use metalanguage to reflect on how grammatical choices influence meaning and establish register in texts.
Intermediate: use metalanguage to compare texts to identify how differences in grammar and text features determine the nature of formal and informal texts.
Advanced: use metalanguage to explain grammatical forms to others.

contentGroups.title: Developing intercultural understanding through target language texts

items.text: Respond to texts by reflecting on how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), practices, values and perspectives
items.examples:
Beginner: consider and discuss how emphasis or perspectives in texts such as documentaries or news reports can reflect cultural context.
Intermediate: consider and compare how language in texts written in the target language is used to express personal and community identity, culture, practices, values and perspectives.
Advanced: analyse and reflect on how identity is expressed across the target language and culture(s), such as the idea of belonging and the importance of cultural group or family membership.

items.text: Respond to texts by reflecting on the relationship between language and culture in communication
items.examples:
Beginner: develop the capability to reflect on and engage with difference.
Intermediate: question and discuss stereotypes found in texts.
Advanced: develop a metalanguage for discussing the relationship between language and culture.

outcomes.description: creates texts for a range of purposes using culturally appropriate modelled language

contentGroups.title: Creating spoken, written and multimodal texts in the target language

items.text: Participate in the creation of texts using known words or phrases
items.examples:
Beginner: choose vocabulary to contribute to a collaborative text.
Beginner: label photographs for a classroom display.
Intermediate: contribute to the creation of a timetable of weekly or monthly activities.
Advanced: collaborate to create a visual Aboriginal seasonal calendar labelled in the target language.

items.text: Create texts using modelled language and/or images
items.examples:
Beginner: participate in creating a visual text accompanied by key vocabulary or modelled language.
Intermediate: participate in completing speech bubbles in a comic strip.
Advanced: create a visual display or digital presentation of a cultural event in the target language.

items.text: Create texts to convey information, experiences or opinions
items.examples:
Beginner: participate in creating a list of ingredients needed for a recipe.
Intermediate: participate in creating a short, introductory speech to introduce themselves to a new classmate.
Advanced: create a simple recount, poem or narrative.

contentGroups.title: Applying knowledge of language systems to create texts in the target language

items.text: Use sounds and expressions of the target language when creating spoken texts
items.examples:
Beginner: use correct intonation and expression when saying key words in the target language.
Intermediate: explore the role of intonation, stress and rhythm when creating spoken texts.

items.text: Identify vocabulary, grammatical structures and/or text features of the target language
items.examples:
Beginner: label or perform familiar verbs in the target language.
Intermediate: use familiar verbs or adjectives.
Intermediate: use appropriate structures and features when asking questions.
Advanced: use appropriate word order when making simple statements.

items.text: Create texts using text features appropriate to the target language
items.examples:
Beginner: match vocabulary in the target language to a familiar text.
Intermediate: complete a scaffold to create a multimodal text, such as a greeting card or digital recipe.
Advanced: create a text on a familiar topic, such as visual display about themselves (including family members or friends), hobbies, likes and dislikes.

items.text: Explore forming script, characters or symbols in the target language
items.examples:
Beginner: form script, characters or symbols in salt or sand, or using moulding clay or dough.
Intermediate: practise the writing system of the target language using models.

items.text: Follow a scaffold to create a text using the target language writing system
items.examples:
Beginner: trace, copy or match words using the target language writing system.
Intermediate: fill in a form or survey to provide information about themselves, such as age, country of birth, Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Nation/Place of birth and/or residence or hobbies.
Advanced: write short texts using the target language writing system.

contentGroups.title: Applying knowledge of the target language culture(s) to create texts

items.text: Use images, signs or symbols to create texts that demonstrate an understanding of culture
items.examples:
Beginner: participate in creating a menu for a specific mealtime.
Intermediate: participate in creating a bilingual dictionary or word wall, using language accompanied by images, signs or symbols.
Advanced: create a visual display or digital presentation comparing a cultural practice from their own or local Aboriginal culture with one from the target language.

items.text: Create texts by selecting and/or using modelled language appropriate to cultural practices
items.examples:
Beginner: use culturally appropriate gestures in spoken texts.
Intermediate: participate in creating posters for the school that celebrate diverse cultural representations.
Advanced: participate in creating a narrative that involves diverse cultural representations.

items.text: Respond in English or the target language to known words or phrases
items.examples:

Beginner: answer simple questions by pointing to a communication board that uses vocabulary in the target language paired with visuals.
Intermediate: respond to information in texts in the target language that relate to other learning areas, such as countries and their capital cities.
Advanced: use key vocabulary to ask questions about a text.

items.text: Share ideas or opinions in the target language or in English in response to texts
items.examples:
Beginner: share likes or dislikes of a text using gestures, images, symbols, signing or modelled language.
Intermediate: share preferences for the ending of a film viewed or story read in class.

items.text: Apply strategies to organise and understand information in texts
items.examples:
Beginner: participate in retelling key events from a familiar story using images and modelled language.
Intermediate: participate in presenting the results of a class survey in various formats, such as list, table or pie chart.
